### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_delegation (symbol, a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via sys_approval_delegation (symbol, a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9fa607a49ef26f55ac0873a8d0a0266ec7107144` — the merge of head `c7cf6654b99ab2d9da5e75445bdbcb8b57c9bc0d` into base `77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9fa607a49ef26f55ac0873a8d0a0266ec7107144 && git checkout 9fa607a49ef26f55ac0873a8d0a0266ec7107144
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4 c7cf6654b99ab2d9da5e75445bdbcb8b57c9bc0d && git checkout -B drift-repro 77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4 && git merge --no-ff c7cf6654b99ab2d9da5e75445bdbcb8b57c9bc0d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 77392e901cce58316e803144971f2741ef049fc4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c7cf6654b99ab2d9da5e75445bdbcb8b57c9bc0d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/ooo-delegation-organization.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/admin-exemption-retired.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-notification-body.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/es-ES.source-hashes.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/ja-JP.source-hashes.generated.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (grantAppliesInTenant, grantOrganizationOf), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (resolveSystemInsertOrganization), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (injectTenantOnInsert), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts (denyOrganizationRemoval), packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts (sys_approval_delegation, fate 3), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts (bindDelegationWriteGuard), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/pre-18-tenant-column.testkit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/default-organization.testkit.ts, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D1, D9, D10, D11), scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, .changeset/24583-7a2-organization-less-grant-readers-retired.md (precedent), and the two prose faces .changeset/25280-delegation-own-organization.md and content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx read for truth to the code

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The own-organization match, `organizationNamed()` on both sides — right.** `organizationNamed(value)` returns `null` for `null`, `undefined` and `''`, else `String(value)`: the same normalization core's module-private `grantOrganizationOf` applies to a grant row's value. The comparison `rowOrg === requestOrg` runs only after `rowOrg === null` has already been diverted to the warn-and-skip branch, so a match needs the row side non-null; and because `requestOrg` is `null` for a request with no organization while `rowOrg` is never `null` at the comparison, a null request matches nothing. That is `grantAppliesInTenant`'s rule (`organizationId !== null && organizationId === tenantId`) read in the same order, with no posture branch, which is ADR-0131 D11. One deliberate non-fork: core's normalizer also reads a camelCase `organizationId` spelling off the row; the plugin's reads the value handed to it, and the delegation read names its columns (`fields: [... 'organization_id']`), so no camelCase row reaches it. No drift.

2. **The request's organization that feeds the comparison — right.** Every `applyOooDelegation` call site (`user`, `field`, `manager`, `expression resolveAs: user`) receives the `organizationId` `expandApprovers` was given, and `openNodeRequest` passes `requestOrg = subjectOrg ?? ctxOrg` (the subject record's organization through the shared `recordOrgResolver`, the acting context as fallback); the fallback and admin-rescue slates pass the same `requestOrg`, and the decide-time re-expansion passes the stored request row's `organization_id`. The new pin "a member signed in to A, opening on B's record, gets no reroute from A's delegation" holds that reading.

3. **An org-less active row warns and never matches; is a legitimate delegation lost? — no, the dev's reach reading holds against the cited code.** Under a wall: a session insert carries `options.tenantId` and `injectTenantOnInsert` fills an empty `organization_id` from it; an elevated or system insert with no organization reaches `Engine.resolveSystemInsertOrganization`, which derives the Default Organization only under `single` and otherwise throws `SystemWriteOrganizationRequiredError` (D9); an update that empties the column is refused by `denyOrganizationRemoval` in both the payload half and the stored-image half of the write wall, gated on `walled`. The delegation write guard (`bindDelegationWriteGuard`) stamps only `delegator_id` and does not touch the organization, so it neither helps nor hurts. So under a wall the only organization-less rows are stored state from before, and `organization-ownership-inventory.ts:538` records `sys_approval_delegation` as `fate: 'attribution'` with no anchor and the `D10_SINGLE` citation ("under single, the Default Organization; otherwise reported"), which is exactly what the PR says: attributed under `single`, reported and left NULL under a wall. Under `single`, D9 derives the Default Organization for the delegation its author writes and for the request's subject record, so an 18.x delegation still applies by construction, and the three `installDefaultOrganization` suites that insert a delegation without an organization (`actor-lookups-hold-ids`, `approval-notification-keyed-text` which now writes `ORG` explicitly, `approval-requested-notification`) pass unchanged on the head's check-runs. Two populations sit outside the PR's "only a database upgraded from before 18.0" sentence and are judged non-blocking: a lean embedding that registers no `sys_organization` (the D9 2026-10-22 note stores NULL there, by design, and no served production composition reaches it), and a `single` store born on 18.0.0 (tenant columns still nullable per the D1 amendment) where an update clears the column outside any wall. In both the row is reported at `warn` with the `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` remedy, which attributes it under `single`, so nothing is silently lost.

4. **Every delegation reader is covered — right.** On the head, `sys_approval_delegation` is read in exactly one place, `lookupActiveDelegation` (`engine.find` at `approval-service.ts:3278`), and `lookupActiveDelegation` has exactly one caller, `applyOooDelegation`. The notification body, the admin-rescue slate and the decide-time re-expansion all consume `applyOooDelegation`'s output (the `substitutions` collector or the returned slate), never the table. `lifecycle-hooks.ts` names the object only for its write guard and its hook-package list; `approvals-plugin.ts` for the nav item; `packages/client/src/index.ts` in a docblock. No second door applies a cross-organization delegation.

5. **The warn — right, and shaped as the card asked.** It fires per skipped active org-less row per lookup, carries `{ delegationId, delegatorId, delegateId, requestOrganizationId }` and the two-posture remedy; `this.logger?.warn?.` matches the file's other warnings. The new pin asserts the kind and the named fields, never the wording.

6. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` — right.** The two new entries (`ooo-delegation-organization.test.ts`, verbs `delete` and `update`, `pinned: 1` each) match the test double, whose `update` opens with `assertEngineUpdateDispatch(data, options)` and whose `delete` opens with `assertEngineDeleteDispatch(options)`; `find` honours `options.limit`. The ledger counts pinned doubles per (file, verb), so `1` is the right count. `Lint and Repo Gates` is green on the head.

7. **The `approvals.mdx` paragraph — true to the code.** "Belongs to the organization it is created in" is `injectTenantOnInsert`/D9; "reroutes only the approvals opened in that organization" is the comparison; "a request's organization is its record's" is `subjectOrg ?? ctxOrg`; "create a delegation in each" follows; "reroutes nothing, and the approval service logs a warning" is the skip branch. The one broad word is "only a database upgraded from before 18.0 can hold" an org-less row (see item 3's two edge populations); not false for any served production composition, and judged non-blocking.

8. **The object help and the four bundles — right.** `en` matches the object's new `description` byte for byte (regenerated). `es-ES` ("La organización a la que pertenece esta delegación. Solo redirige las aprobaciones abiertas en esta organización."), `ja-JP` ("この委任が属する組織です。この組織で開始された承認だけを振り替えます。") and `zh-CN` ("此委派所属的组织。它只改派在该组织中发起的审批。") each say what the English says. The `es-ES` and `ja-JP` source-hash entries for `objects.sys_approval_delegation.fields.organization_id.help` drop, which is what the companion's own header prescribes for a leaf that stops being a byte copy ("Re-translate the leaf ... the next extract drops its entry by itself"); `zh-CN` already carried no entry for that path. The claim (6365085992) said `es-ES`/`ja-JP` would be left as the tool's byte copies; the PR hand-translated them instead and says so in its body. A stricter outcome than the claim, not a breach.

9. **The edited tests kept what they pinned — right.** `admin-exemption-retired`: `seedDelegation` now writes `organization_id: 't1'` (the submitter's organization in that suite) and the suite's assertion, that a delegation cannot rescue an in-flight approval, is untouched. `admin-rescue-named-slate`: `dlg_admin` writes `ORG` and `sys_approval_delegation` leaves the `relaxTenantColumns` list, so the table keeps its NOT NULL column and the insert must carry the organization, which it does; the assertion (an out-of-office administrator is covered by their delegate) is untouched. `approval-notification-body`: `dlg_1`/`dlg_2` write `orgOfDeal('ooo')`/`orgOfDeal('ooo_gone')` and the table leaves the relaxed list; the notification-body assertions are untouched. `approval-service.test`: the one pin that stated the retired reading ("applies a cross-tenant (null org) rule regardless of request tenant") is replaced by its inverse and additionally asserts no `ooo_substitute` audit action was written. Nothing was loosened; each re-stamp moves the fixture onto the organization the request lands in.

10. **The new pin file carries the card's acceptance.** Under `isolated` and `group`: A's delegation does not reroute in B and the request lands in B; the same-organization delegation still applies with the audit comment unchanged; the record's organization wins over the acting context's; an org-less row reroutes nothing in either organization and is reported once per lookup with the named fields; blank and absent count as org-less; the same-organization row applies beside an org-less one; a chain stops at an org-less hop; a request with no organization takes none. Under `single`: the Default-Organization delegation reroutes; an org-less row does not and is reported. The `single` org-less case is the fate-3 "stored state from before the ceremony" population, correctly framed.

11. **Public surface.** No export is added or changed: `organizationNamed` is module-private; `lookupActiveDelegation` stays private; `packages/core` and `packages/spec` are untouched; no schema, no governed path. What narrows is which stored rows reroute an approval. The accept set of `sys_approval_delegation` is unchanged (every row a caller could write before is still accepted).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/25280-delegation-own-organization.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, a `**BREAKING**` banner, FROM/TO stated in prose and the operator remedy per posture. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. **Right.**
- `no`: no published accept set or public surface widens (item 11). `(narrowing)`: a published behaviour is withdrawn, the help text "null = applies across tenants for this delegator" and the reroute it described. `Metadata-protocol: none`: `sys_approval_delegation` holds runtime data, no authorable key moves. Per AGENTS.md ("the level follows the kind alone ... `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition") the level is `patch`. **Right.**
- Precedent `.changeset/24583-7a2-organization-less-grant-readers-retired.md` is `yes (narrowing)` at `minor` because it moved exported readers in `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` (public surface); this PR moves none, so `no (narrowing)` at `patch` is the consistent reading of the same break on a package that exports nothing new.
- ADR-0087 marker: the category exists in ADR-0087's closed vocabulary; the body's FROM/TO is prose with no arrow and no code-span rewrite pair, so the catch-all is not refused by the prescription detector, and `Lint and Repo Gates` (which runs `check:adr-0087-registration`) and `Check Changeset` are both green on the head. **Right.**
- The narrowing face: `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the file list decides no path face and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `(narrowing)`, so `--face narrowing` and `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the served tier. Consistent with the brief.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in the os-dev-report (6367007163). `out_of_scope_findings`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, PR body "Acceptance notes": the branch is the harness-assigned `claude/project-thread-4a6wrl`, not `claude/issue-25280-...`. The claim comments (6364952044, 6365085992) are the identity record and name that branch; the check-run "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is green. Answered.
- Dev flag: #25342 (delegator prefill) edits the same object file and bundles; whichever lands second merges main and regenerates. "No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path" is green on the head. Answered, no action here.
- Dev flag: no automated rewrite is offered for a walled org-less row because the row names nothing to attribute it by. Matches inventory fate 3 for this table (no anchor). Answered.
- Dev flag (claim, superseding): the `(narrowing)` arm owes one full dogfood battery on the final head. The head's check-runs show `Dogfood Regression Gate` success with the three shards, `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` skipped by design; the full battery evidence is the os-dev-report's `dogfood_battery` line (`os-verify-lock` on `c7cf6654b`, 290 files passed, 3 skipped, 2494 tests passed, 18 skipped, no failures). Recorded as the dev's measurement; the check-runs on the head answer every derived gate family.
- Reviewer observation, non-blocking: the "only a database upgraded from before 18.0 can hold" sentence (docs and changeset) is broader than the code guarantees for two populations outside any served production composition (item 3); the warn and its remedy cover both. No change asked.
- Check-runs on `c7cf6654b99ab2d9da5e75445bdbcb8b57c9bc0d`: 42, every one `success` or `skipped` by design; none failed.
